turns.text: Thanks for sharing. Give me a moment to digest the file. Then I’ll follow up with a question.
The procedure describes a quarterly schedule review about 30 days before quarter end, followed by invoice drafting and client confirmation. Is that the process you carry out today?
Yes, that file is our written procedure and most of it is still right.
You mentioned that most of the procedure is still right; which parts, if any, no longer match how the work is done today?

One correction to the file: step 2, draft and internally review invoices, is no longer done the way the file says. Since this quarter the team lead does that step herself in a shared tracker and emails me when it is finished, so I only start my part after her email arrives. Everything else in the file is current.
What does the team lead check in the shared tracker before emailing you that the step is finished?

After that, we obtain client approval and send invoices. That is done by: One Rock fund team or client approves; the GPFS preparer sends the. We use Sage drafts and email or another approved delivery channel for it. The check on it: the invoices sent and their amounts must match the approved drafts.

Then, we post invoices and recognize revenue. That is done by: GPFS preparer and reviewer. We use Sage and the central schedule for it. The check on it: the posted invoices and accounting entry must match the approved list and posting date.
Who is accountable for the overall monitoring-fee billing and revenue-recognition process?
This capture still has open sections. 15 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.

topics.answer: The work is called Monitoring Fee Billing & Revenue Recognition; the procedure identifies it as MC-04.
The procedure describes billing portfolio companies for monitoring fees and recording the related receivable and revenue.

The procedure schedules the review approximately 30 days before quarter end, invoice delivery typically around the 15th before quarter end, and posting on the first business day of the quarter.
The event or person initiating the schedule review, and whether the stated dates are fixed deadlines, are not established.

Documented outputs include approved invoices sent, posted receivables and revenue, cleared prepayments, a posted reconciled offset, a fund-team report and an up-to-date receivable-exceptions log.
The overall cycle's final closure condition and treatment of outstanding receivables remain to be confirmed.
The role accountable for the overall result is not identified; the procedure names preparers and reviewers but does not establish overall accountability.

The procedure says the GPFS management company preparer reviews each company, contact, fee and fund using the current schedule, agreements and investment or exit information. The preparer confirms changes and billing status with the One Rock fund team, checks agreement coverage and separately records outside-Sage invoices and client holds, producing a client-confirmed billing list.
Since this quarter the team lead handles draft and internal invoice review herself in a shared tracker and emails the participant when finished; the participant starts their part after that email. For the next step, the procedure says drafts go to the One Rock fund team for approval, changes are resolved in the schedule and drafts, and the preparer sends approved invoices to portfolio companies and retains approval and delivery evidence.
The procedure directs the GPFS preparer and reviewer to post approved Sage invoices on the approved date, normally recording Dr 1100 / Cr 4005, and compare posted totals with the approved schedule, resolving differences.
For verified cash received before posting, the documented route identifies the future invoice, records Dr Cash / Cr 2100 on receipt and Dr 2100 / Cr 4005 on the invoice date, then records and closes or applies the prepayment to the invoice. Cash, invoice status and accounts 1100, 2100 and 4005 are compared to prevent duplicate receivable or revenue. Unidentified cash or payments after the invoice date follow normal receivable and cash-application rules.
At month-end close the documented GPFS preparer and reviewer compare account 4005 activity to support, enter fees into the offset spreadsheet, check ownership and LP percentages and fund factors against current management-fee workpapers, apply the approved formula and factor by fund and portfolio company, and post Dr 4015 / Cr 2205. The procedure requires reconciling the accrual against the list of fees and revenue and resolving differences.
The procedure has the GPFS management company preparer provide the Monitoring Fees Received Report to the fund team at least twice quarterly, communicate investment and fee changes, maintain classifications, review aging with One Rock, document collection, hold and write-off decisions, and track manual invoices on the central schedule.
The written procedure says the outside-Sage invoice preparation procedure is undocumented and work must not proceed without an approved manual procedure. The exact Sage steps to apply or close a prepayment also need confirmation.
The participant says One Rock fund team or client approves, and the GPFS preparer sends the invoices using Sage drafts and email or another approved delivery channel.

The procedure prohibits drafting from unsupported or outdated schedule lines and directs unclear agreement coverage or status to the client and accounting owner. Sent invoices and amounts must match approved drafts, and client hold instructions must be documented before sending or posting.
The procedure requires posted invoices and entries to match the approved list and posting date; report, revenue, offset and aging lists and totals must agree. Write-off requires specific client instruction and an approved accounting entry.
What the team lead checks in the shared tracker before emailing that step 2 is finished remains unclear.
The participant says the posted invoices and accounting entry must match the approved list and posting date; the GPFS preparer and reviewer perform posting and revenue recognition.

The procedure describes different handling for genuine pre-invoice cash, client-directed delayed revenue, and manual invoices outside Sage; these are conditional routes rather than evidence of a general client variant.

The written procedure references a central monitoring-fee schedule, supporting agreements, Sage invoice drafts, client approvals and sent records, cash records, an offset spreadsheet, management-fee workpapers, the Monitoring Fees Received Report and Sage aging report. A broken, draft, incomplete or unapproved client workbook or example is not an official source under the procedure.
The team lead uses a shared tracker for the changed draft and internal review step and emails the participant when it is finished.

The participant identifies the file as the team's written procedure and says everything except the changed step 2 is current.
The participant says step 2 changed this quarter and everything else in the file is current.
The documented route involves GPFS management company staff, One Rock, portfolio companies and associated funds.
Whether the One Rock route reflects a general GPFS standard remains unclear.

The procedure states that current approved policy recognizes the full normal invoice amount as revenue on the invoice date, not over three months; a client instruction to delay revenue requires specifically approved accounting treatment.
The procedure requires quarterly review of offset percentages and factors against the LPA and another comparison source whose binding is unclear in the extraction; the entry must match recognized revenue. It prohibits use of the formula or factor table until the owner, approved version, LPA basis and sign convention are confirmed.
The approved offset formula, factor-table owner and version, LPA basis and sign convention need confirmation; one required reconciliation and comparison source is unclear in the extracted procedure.

The documented offset calculation consumes current management-fee workpapers for ownership, LP percentages and fund factors.
The documented process sends draft invoices to the One Rock fund team or client for approval and provides the Monitoring Fees Received Report to the fund team.
The exact relationship to MC-05 is unclear in the extracted procedure.

The procedure uses Sage for drafts, posting and aging; an offset spreadsheet for the accrual calculation; a central schedule for billing and manual-invoice tracking; and email or another approved channel for delivery.
Step 2 is now handled in a shared tracker; the participant says Sage and the central schedule are used to post invoices and recognize revenue.

The procedure specifies a Monitoring Fees Received Report to the fund team at least twice per quarter.
Transaction counts and effort remain unestablished.

steps.title: Calculate offset accrual
steps.description: Apply the approved formula and factor for each fund and portfolio company.

steps.title: Post and reconcile offset
steps.system: Sage, offset spreadsheet and management-fee workpapers

steps.description: Track manual and outside-Sage invoices on the central schedule.

The procedure identifies sent approved invoices, posted receivables and revenue, reconciled offsets, a fund-team report and an up-to-date receivables exception log. Which combined condition closes the overall work, and all downstream consumers, are UNKNOWN.
